claims.text: Ethanol oxidation activity on nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts is governed by the local surface atomic arrangement.
Increasing the relative surface concentration of Rh enhances water adsorption and activation.
Rh-assisted water activation forms reactive hydroxyl species that promote ethanol oxidation at lower overpotentials.
The equiatomic nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs baseline is a solid solution with a uniform elemental distribution.
Increasing bulk Rh content while holding particle size and synthesis conditions fixed will enhance Rh surface segregation or local clustering.
Rh-enriched surface regions provide an increased density of oxophilic sites responsible for water dissociation.
Increasing Rh surface concentration increases the oxophilicity of the catalyst surface.
Greater surface oxophilicity promotes adsorbed OH formation at lower overpotentials.
Adsorbed OH facilitates ethanol oxidation by mitigating catalyst poisoning.
Adsorbed OH enables faster formation of key ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Relative to the equiatomic baseline, Rh-enriched catalysts will have a lower ethanol-oxidation onset potential.
Relative to the equiatomic baseline, Rh-enriched catalysts will produce higher current density at a given applied potential.
Rh enrichment may improve selectivity toward desired ethanol-oxidation products.
The proposed mechanism should apply to nanoscale solid-solution catalysts in acidic electrolyte between 0.0 and 1.0 V versus RHE.
Water activation plays a significant role in ethanol oxidation within the stated potential window.

contradictions.description: PtPdRhRuIrOs contains six named elements, whereas the material_initial_state describes a uniform distribution of 'all seven elements.'
